title: Slow Cooker Chickpea & Carrot Curry Stew
description: Chickpeas, carrots, and tomatoes simmer into a mild pantry-friendly slow cooker stew with simple curry seasoning.
substitutions: Use white beans instead of chickpeas.
Use frozen sliced carrots without thawing.
Use regular milk for a milder, less coconut-forward stew.

steps.text: Add the stew ingredients to the slow cooker.
Cook until the carrots are tender.
Stir in the milk and finish.

cookSteps.text: Add 2 cans chickpeas, 3 sliced carrots, 1 can diced tomatoes, 1 1/2 cups broth, 1 1/2 teaspoons curry powder, 1/2 teaspoon garlic powder, and 1/4 teaspoon salt to the slow cooker. Stir.
Cover and cook on HIGH for about 4 hours, until the carrots are tender.
Stir in 1/2 cup milk or coconut milk. Cover for 5 minutes to warm through, then taste and adjust seasoning.

storage: Refrigerate up to 4 days or freeze up to 2 months.

title: Sheet-Pan Sweet Potato & Black Bean Nachos
description: Roasted sweet potato rounds get topped with black beans and cheese for an easy sheet-pan dinner or hearty snack.

ingredients.item: sweet potatoes, sliced into thin rounds

substitutions: Use pinto beans instead of black beans.
Use Monterey Jack instead of cheddar.
Serve with plain yogurt instead of sour cream if desired.

cookSteps.text: Heat the oven to 425°F. Toss 2 sliced sweet potatoes with 1 tablespoon oil and 1/2 teaspoon chili powder on a sheet pan and spread into one layer.
Roast for 20–25 minutes, flipping once, until tender and browned at the edges.
Scatter 1 can black beans and 1 cup shredded cheddar over the potatoes. Bake 5 more minutes, until the beans are hot and cheese is melted.
Spoon 1/2 cup salsa over the top if using and serve warm.

storage: Refrigerate leftovers up to 3 days. Reheat on a sheet pan or in an air fryer for the best texture.

title: Leftover Rice, Tuna & Cabbage Bowls
description: Cold leftover rice, tuna, and crunchy cabbage become a quick savory lunch bowl with a simple soy dressing.
substitutions: Use canned chicken instead of tuna.
Use shredded carrots for part of the cabbage.
Use a splash of vinegar if you do not have lime or lemon.

cookSteps.text: Heat 1 teaspoon oil in a small skillet over medium heat. Add 2 cups leftover rice and cook, stirring, for about 5 minutes until steaming hot.
Divide the hot rice between 2 bowls. Top with 1 drained can tuna and 1 1/2 cups sliced cabbage.
Drizzle each bowl with the 1 tablespoon soy sauce and 1 teaspoon lime or lemon juice if using. Toss lightly before eating.

storage: Refrigerate components separately up to 2 days. Reheat rice thoroughly before serving leftovers.

title: Small-Batch Chocolate Oatmeal Cookies
description: A small tray of chewy oatmeal cookies gets a little cocoa and uses ordinary baking staples when a full batch is too much.
substitutions: Use quick oats if that is what you have.
Skip the chocolate chips for a simple cocoa-oat cookie.
Use white sugar instead of brown sugar; the cookies will be a little crisper.

cookSteps.text: Heat the oven to 350°F. Mix 3 tablespoons softened butter with 1/4 cup brown sugar, then mix in 1 egg yolk.
Stir in 1/4 cup flour, 1 tablespoon cocoa powder, and 1/4 teaspoon baking soda. Fold in 1/2 cup oats and 2 tablespoons chocolate chips if using.
Scoop 6 cookies onto a baking sheet, flatten slightly, and bake 10–12 minutes until the edges are set.

storage: Keep covered at room temperature up to 3 days or freeze up to 1 month.
